About us
ACCELQ is the only cloud-based continuous testing platform that seamlessly automates API and web testing without writing a single line of code. IT teams of all sizes use ACCELQ to accelerate their testing by automating critical aspects of lifecycle like test design, planning, test generation, and execution.

A few highlights:
- Codeless natural language Functional, API Automation
- No IDE, Fully browser-based 
- Visualize and drive quality with ACCELQ Universe
- Design/Automate/Maintain your testing 3X Faster

ACCELQ was analyzed as leader in the latest Continuous Test Automation platform Forrester research. ACCELQ customers are Fortune 500 enterprises across industry verticals globally, and they have adopted ACCELQ to significantly accelerate their automation objectives. ACCELQ is proven to speed up automation development by 3 times and bring down the maintenance 70% that translates to over 50% of cost savings and enables alignment with continuous delivery.

Your testing stack shouldn’t be harder to manage than the software you’re testing.

Modern applications span web, mobile, APIs, and multiple layers of technology. QA teams shouldn’t have to navigate a different workflow every time they move from one to another.

That’s where a unified approach to testing changes the equation.

With ACCELQ Unified, teams can bring different testing needs into one connected quality ecosystem, so they can spend less time managing the process and more time improving what matters: quality, coverage, and speed.

And when AI agents are working alongside your team 24/7, the possibilities go even further.

The future of testing could give testers more room for the work that matters.
Kasturi Rajamanikkam
, Senior QA Engineer and AI enthusiast, believes AI can be a massive opportunity for the testing community.

From moving beyond coded automation to embracing codeless testing, to automating regression and smoke suites across 30+ CMS-based websites, Kasturi shares how her approach to automation has evolved with ACCELQ.

And with self-healing helping reduce maintenance, there’s more room for testers to focus on strategy, complex business logic, edge cases, and quality.
Because the goal isn’t to replace the tester.

It’s to give testers more time to do what they do best.

4 signals your open-source test automation may be reaching its limit:

1️⃣ Maintenance is eating into coverage time
2️⃣ Your toolchain is becoming fragmented
3️⃣ Automation depends on a handful of specialists
4️⃣ CI/CD integration needs constant rework

If two or more are showing up consistently, it may be time to revisit your automation strategy.

Our latest blog explores the Maintenance Crossover Point and what comes next.
